Parameter specification

Source: R/family-spec.R
par_spec.Rd

Describes one parameter of a distribution: its domain, links, role and how it enters regression. Used when defining distributions with custom_family().

Usage

par_spec(
  name,
  domain = "real",
  role = "shape",
  link = NULL,
  links = NULL,
  symbol = name,
  is_mean = FALSE,
  offset_allowed = FALSE,
  regression = TRUE,
  data = FALSE,
  interpretation = "",
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  default = NULL,
  estimate = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Parameter name used in formulas and distribution().

domain

One of "real", "positive", "nonneg", "unit", "circular", "greater_than_one", "greater_than_two", "positive_integer", "nonneg_integer", "integer", "unit_closed" or "any".

role

Free text role such as "location", "scale", "shape", "dispersion", "rate", "skewness", "tail", "inflation" or "mixing".

link

Default link name.

links

Allowed link names.

symbol

Mathematical symbol for documentation.

is_mean

TRUE only when the parameter equals the expectation of the response for every parameter value. Never inferred from the name.

offset_allowed

Whether an offset may enter this parameter's predictor.

regression

Whether the parameter may have a predictor. Fixed data arguments such as binomial trials use FALSE together with data = TRUE.

data

TRUE for data arguments (for example the number of trials).

interpretation

Text shown in documentation.

lower, upper

Optional numeric bounds overriding the domain.

default

Optional value used by distribution() when omitted.

estimate

For a non regression parameter, "ordered" or "free" to estimate it as a vector whose length comes from the response (ordinal thresholds); NULL otherwise.

Value

An object of class regcomp_par.

Examples

par_spec("mu", "positive", role = "location", is_mean = TRUE)
#> <parameter mu> domain positive, role location, link log, equals the mean
